issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/1632
Originally posted by **krauss** May 10, 2022 Hey guys, I've been using Starlette with FastAPI and Strawberry to expose a GraphQL API for my web app. However, since last week I noticed I'm getting the error below when trying to acess http://localhost:8000/graphql: ```python INFO: 127.0.0.1:45822 - "GET /graphql HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error ERROR: Exception in ASGI application Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/venv/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/uvicorn/protocols/http/httptools_impl.py", line 372, in run_asgi result = await app(self.scope, self.receive, self.send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/venv/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/uvicorn/middleware/proxy_headers.py", line 75, in __call__ return await self.app(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./fastapi/applications.py", line 269, in __call__ await super().__call__(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/applications.py", line 124, in __call__ await self.middleware_stack(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/middleware/errors.py", line 184, in __call__ raise exc File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/middleware/errors.py", line 162, in __call__ await self.app(scope, receive, _send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/middleware/cors.py", line 84, in __call__ await self.app(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/exceptions.py", line 93, in __call__ raise exc File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/exceptions.py", line 82, in __call__ await self.app(scope, receive, sender) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./fastapi/middleware/asyncexitstack.py", line 21, in __call__ raise e File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./fastapi/middleware/asyncexitstack.py", line 18, in __call__ await self.app(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/routing.py", line 665, in __call__ await route.handle(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/routing.py", line 261, in handle await self.app(scope, receive, send) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./strawberry/asgi/__init__.py", line 47, in __call__ await self.http_handler_class( File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./strawberry/asgi/handlers/http_handler.py", line 42, in handle sub_response = Response( File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/responses.py", line 55, in __init__ self.init_headers(headers) File "/home/jrkrauss/OpenSource/Workspaces/python/ceprol-back/./starlette/responses.py", line 85, in init_headers and not (self.status_code < 200 or self.status_code in (204, 304)) TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` These are some of the libraries I'm using: fastapi==0.77.0 starlette==0.20.0 strawberry==0.111.2 graphql-core==3.2.1 uvicorn==0.17.6 uvloop==0.16.0 After debugging the libraries, I noticed that the chunk of code below, taken from file [response.py, line 84](https://github.com/encode/starlette/blob/e7a92ee4cd43b6d7acf4e2fdedb20fe0e86f9620/starlette/responses.py#L84) is causing the error : ```python body = getattr(self, "body", None) if ( body is not None and populate_content_length and not (self.status_code < 200 or self.status_code in (204, 304)) ): ``` To summarize, the error above happens when `self.status_code is None`. This is how to fix it: ```python body = getattr(self, "body", None) if ( body is not None and self.status_code is not None and populate_content_length and not (self.status_code < 200 or self.status_code in (204, 304)) ): ``` Should I open a PR to fix it or is this something that's already on your radar? Cheers!
issue.title: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int' on trying to acess http://localhost:8000/graphql
